After watching "The Long Way Round," Bryon put Mongolia on the top of his bucket list of places to travel. It was a quick decision to join Rally for Rangers after finding out he could ride motorcycles and do something valuable for the national parks of Mongolia and across the world. Bryon has participated in multiples rallies in Mongolia, Namibia, and Nepal.

Riders by Rally.Name: Dave Ray - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Dave, a father of 6 and about to be a grandfather of two, spends his time when not working with his wife Sue & family. As time allows Dave is an avid Power Sports freak, restoring and riding all manner of vehicles. His favorite being Boats and Motorcycles. Growing up in Toronto Canada in the 80s, Dave stayed out of trouble fixing and riding Motorcycles both dirt and road. Dave was lucky enough to work at Kelly’s Motorcycle in Brampton during High School and University where they supported him by letting Dave purchase a bike each spring at cost, then sell it in the fall to pay for the semesters’ books! While Motorcycles are a passion Dave’s first love is performance boats where he has traveled all over North America, Europe, Russia, India and the Middle East crewing for Formula1 Boat Racing teams (F1H2O & CHAMP series). As recent empty nesters Dave has returned his to motorcycle roots having just purchased 2024 Yamaha

Riders by Rally.Name: Domenic DeVincenzi 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Beginning with an old Honda XR100 on a Northern California ranch, Domenic's thirst for adventure, freedom, and speed was born. An XR250 soon followed, then a couple of those orange bikes, and way too many KLRs, among others… but all of this has resulted in countless thousands of miles of exploring the world and enjoying life on two wheels. Domenic would eventually spend time in Rwanda to support the expansion of life-saving, medical drone delivery operations there, and would embark on East African mini adventures on small, Indian-made motorcycles that wholeheartedly embodied the phrase "safety third". So, what do you get when you combine a passion for travel, motorcycles, and affecting positive global change? The Rally for Rangers! National parks, public lands, and those that support and protect them are so vitally important to our modern world, and the decision to assist in that mission was an obvious one from the moment Domenic first heard about the organization in Death Valley in 2021. Domenic's first Rally for Rangers was in Peru in 2022, but last year’s Mongolia ride really set the hook and he’s back again this year!

Riders by Rally.Name: Donald E. Johnson 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Introducing Donald E. Johnson, whose retirement has become a canvas for his passion-driven adventures. A man of few words, but with a zany humor – he responded to his application by saying that he rides motorcycles only because his wife lets him. As he joins his second Rally for Rangers in Mongolia, his excitement is palpable. Eager to connect with fellow riders and share the open road, Donald's warm spirit promises to light up the journey. Beyond the world of motorcycles, his devotion extends to family. A proud father of a daughter and a doting grandfather to a young grandson, Donald's love forms the cornerstone of his adventurous life. His zest for exploration extends to the great outdoors, both in snow and sunshine. When the white landscapes beckon, Donald finds his thrill in snowmobiling, carving his way through the pristine trails. And when the snow melts, his adventure bike becomes his faithful companion, ready to conquer new horizons.

Riders by Rally.Name: Elias Bikahi - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Elias Bikahi became interested in participating in the Rally for Rangers after assisting with a fundraiser for fellow rider, Tom Medema. This was his fourth time riding out to support those preserving nature around the world - Mongolia 2015, Patagonia 2018, and Peru 2022. He's committed to supporting the rangers protecting our wild spaces by providing them with resources to support their work and our planet.

Riders by Rally.Name: Enife Kelly - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: With a passion for motorcycles, biking, and all things outdoors, Enife is always on the lookout for her next thrilling escapade. In fact, she's been daydreaming about joining the Rally for Rangers ever since her buddies Anna Kim and Oliver Dunkley couldn't stop raving about it! But Enife is more than just an adrenaline junkie. She's a true entrepreneur at heart, having rocked the role of an Engineering Program Manager at Apple and a Producer at Microsoft. With her sharp mind and go-getter attitude, she's no stranger to pushing boundaries and bringing amazing ideas to life. When Enife isn't conquering the corporate world, you'll find her unleashing her inner warrior in the most unexpected ways. She's a Krav Maga aficionado, a kickboxing enthusiast, and a fearless practitioner of MMA and BJJ. There's no doubt that she's always up for a challenge and loves testing her limits. But don't be fooled by her fierce fighting skills and impressive professional background – Enife's curiosity knows no bounds. She's a lifelong learner who's constantly seeking new knowledge and experiences. Whether it's mastering a new skill or diving deep into a fascinating subject, Enife is always eager to expand her horizons. 👩🏼‍💻 Engineering Program Manager, Emerging Technology 👩🏼‍🎓 Oxford Univeristy 🏍 Throttle Junkie 🥋 Krav Maga + 🩰 Ballet Enthusiast 📸 Model in A Prior Life

Riders by Rally.Name: Graham Cashwell 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: The motorcycle bug bit him in 1984 when he was a Peace Corps Volunteer in Liberia, West Africa. Riding amidst the challenges of unpaved roads and changing seasons, Graham's initiation into motorcycling was nothing short of a thrilling ride. The idea of adventure riding was introduced to him while traversing Mali, where he crossed paths with the iconic Paris Dakar Rally. This electrifying encounter set his spirit on fire, a spark that still burns bright. Graham's ride of choice now includes a BMW F800 GSA and a KTM 350 EXC-F – machines built to conquer uncharted paths. From BDRs (Backcountry Discovery Routes) to Baja and the rugged terrains of West Virginia, Graham finds solace in the embrace of the open road. Born and raised in the captivating landscapes of Richmond, VA, his heart found home in the allure of the world. With a life that's been lived around the globe, he's woven his experiences into every twist of the throttle. Beyond the road, his journey extends to the skies. A former military pilot turned airline captain, Graham's passion for flying is matched only by his love for two-wheeled exploration. And amidst it all, two remarkable adult children stand as a testament to the legacy he's building. Following his first Rally for Rangers, Mongolia 2023, he gears up for his second adventure in Mongolia, Graham is not only seeking to ride, but to give back. His enthusiasm extends to working with fellow riders and the Mongol Ecology Center, a testament to his deep-rooted commitment to a greater cause.

Riders by Rally.Name: Jake Orpin - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Jake Orpin is a young and enthusiastic gearhead who at 22 years old, is already making waves as a Mechanical Engineering student, constantly tinkering with tools and expanding his knowledge of all things mechanical. Jake's quite handy with tools and when he's not working on mechanical or engineering projects, you'll find Jake indulging in his newfound passion for mountain biking. He's recently been captivated by the thrill of pedaling through rugged terrains, exploring nature's wonders on two wheels. But the adventure doesn't end there for Jake. As a co-owner, along with his father, of a small herd of dual sport and adventure motorcycles, he's well-versed in the world of two-wheeled exploration. Whether it's tackling off-road trails or embarking on daring journeys, Jake is no stranger to the thrill of the ride. Joining forces with his father, Jake is set to embark on the his second Rally for Rangers , his first in Namibia 2023. Their shared love for adventure and the open road will undoubtedly strengthen the bond between father and son as they navigate the challenging landscapes of Lake Hovsgol together.

Riders by Rally.Name: Jason Oliver - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Brewer, second-time Rally for Rangers rally participant, punster, historian, explorer, outlaw, imbiber, adventurer, cultural attaché, small dog owner, motorcycle enthusiast, philosopher, spiritual guru , and smart ass have been all words used to describe Jason Oliver. Most often by himself or when authorities are present. Jason Oliver's first foray into motor bikes was as a twelve year old in 1984 with a fourth hand Sears 2.5hp mini bike. He loved that thing. It had a metal plate that pressed against the rear wheel as a brake, it was sweet. Then came the 1977 Honda XL75 and the 1978 Honda XR80, alongside a slew of mopeds and scooters(Honda, Jawa, Tomos, ect). Anything he could work on while knowing absolutely nothing about mechanics. About 15 years ago he sold his beloved 2001 Kymco People 50 urban destroyer (aka The Silver Bullet) and moved from downtown Washington DC to the Blue Ridge mountains of Virginia. He immediately bought a used Suzuki DRZ 400 dual sport and began exploring the area which was an eye opener (to ride legally!!). His life changed again when he bought his first twin cylinder bike in 2016. He went down the rabbit hole of bigger is better and bought a BMW R1200 GSA. He put some serious miles on it. Crossing the country multiple times, an unofficial Iron Butt challenge, and taking it some places where he shouldn't have but managing to get out every time! Jason still loves large twins but his current favorite bike is a 2023 Honda CT125 Trail bike! If Rally for Rangers has taught him anything, it's that small bikes are a ton of fun and are way more practical in the real world than behemoths. He considers himself blessed to have both small & large displacement bikes, but if he had to choose, he'd pick a smaller bike like the ones donated by Rally for Rangers.

Riders by Rally.Name: Jonathan Orpin - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: At 67 years young, Jonathan Orpin is proving that age is just a number when it comes to chasing thrilling experiences. Jonathan may have only been riding motorcycles for a mere 3 1/2 years, but he's already accomplished some jaw-dropping feats. Just recently, he embarked on a solo journey along the Trans-America Trail, conquering a staggering 2,200 miles from the Pacific all the way into Colorado. Jonathan's riding skills may be moderate, but his determination and unwavering spirit make up for any challenge that comes his way. After founding his timber framing and millwork company 35 years ago, he recently made the exciting decision to sell it to his dedicated employees. While he remains the CEO, he's determined to embrace a more leisurely pace of work and make room for thrilling escapades like the Rally for Rangers. And guess what? Jonathan's son, Jake, will be joining him on this incredible adventure, his second Rally for Rangers. The Orpin duo is ready to create lifelong memories and bond over their shared passion for exploration.

Riders by Rally.Name: Michael Emrich - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Michael (Mike) Emrich, now 75, has been riding since he was only 12 years old. He had traveled by motorcycle around the United States, twice to Alaska and Baja, Canada, Mexico, South America and Newfoundland. He began riding with Rally for Rangers in 2022 on the Bhutan rally. Since then, he joined the Namibia 2023 and Black Hills 2023 rally at the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota. In 2019, Michael embarked on an awe-inspiring journey from Cusco, Peru to Ushuaia, Argentina, covering a staggering 8,700 miles. Over half of the trip was spent conquering dirt, sand, gravel, and muddy roads. It's no surprise that Michael is still in top-notch shape and always ready for new challenges. " Retirement has given me the opportunity to give back to those less fortunate than myself and help with protect and save some of our environment and resources. Rally for Rangers provides the unique experiences of visiting those who you are helping while exploring the country your donation is helping. You also meet people who have similar goals. The group of people you get to travel with are amazing and so helpful." He has been married for 54 years with two beautiful children aged 48 and 45. He holds a BS from California Polytechnic University San Luis Obispo, CA. in Industrial Technology. In, 1975 he founded Solarponics , Inc an Atascadero, CA based Solar Energy, Radiant Heating and Energy Related Design and Installation Company.

Riders by Rally.Name: Seth San Filippo - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Seth San Filippo has had a lifelong passion for motorcycles from a young age. He started on a super cool Mickey Thompson mini bike (that he still has and rides), and quickly graduated to dirt bikes—forming sketchy jumps, scars, and the two-member “Daredevil Club” with his cousin Everest. Nowadays, Seth might be found roaming the logging roads and trails on a long Oregon summer day looking for abandoned fire lookouts on his KLR650. In the winter, he may be in Baja, Mexico with his DRZ400 in search of stellar desert riding, spearfishing, and delicious tacos. In between he could be in a vintage enduro race on his 74’ Suzuki TS250, blowing off steam leaning into the back road corners on his Harley Springer, or competing in the one-day, 100-mile, off-road, Gambler mini bike rally. Basically, Seth is happiest and feels the most alive and free on two wheels in far away places, with music in his helmet speakers and his soul singing. So when he heard about Rally For Rangers on his favorite podcast, Adventure Rider Radio, the cause and the adventure called to him. Seth is beyond excited and honored to be a part of the team and to do his part to help protect the wild places that he cherishes so much. When Seth is not out adventuring on a motorcycle or with his amazing kids Finn (17) and Anna (15), he is very busy as the owner of Urban Lumber Co. (urbanlumber.co) and Urban Hardwoods (urbanhardwoods.com) where he and his crew build beautiful custom furniture from salvaged city trees of the Pacific Northwest.

Riders by Rally.Name: Steven Croft 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Steven participated in the Mongolia 2023 Rally for Rangers and is back for his second Rally for Rangers. His riding journey began with an old orange Yamaha AG175 2 stroke, gifted by his dad in the late 1970s when he was just 14. Since that exhilarating start, Steven's passion for riding has taken him through various terrains and bikes, from enduro and trials to road and now adventure riding. " I p articipated in the 2023 Mongolian Rally and thoroughly enjoyed the whole experience and was a high point of my year. It was v ery well run and managed and now looking forward to doing it again in 2024 with some 2023 friends and new people and riding in a different part of Mongolia. Can't wait for it. At home I'm still riding Suzuki DR650 and V-Strom 1000 plus a HD Fat Bob and enjoy adventure riding in Australia mainly around SE Queensland and Nothern NSW. "

Riders by Rally.Name: Tom Medema - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Tom Medema developed a passion for national parks at a young age on family vacations throughout the American west. This passion turned into a career as a park ranger spanning nearly 30 years. Tom is equally passionate about national parks and public lands around the world and has worked with parks and monuments in South America and Europe as a subject matter expert in the field of interpretation and education. The opportunity to support the protection of natural and cultural heritage of parks and protected areas around the world is an opportunity he is excited and humbled to be a part of. Tom is a sports and outdoor enthusiast, spending much of his free time enjoying two-wheeled travel by mountain bike, road bike, and motorbike. Over the past 20 years he has owned Harley-Davidson and BMW bikes and is currently riding an F800GS on the back roads and trails of Maryland, Virginia and West Virginia in preparation for the next epic and compelling adventure protecting the worlds special places one motorcycle at a time.

Riders by Rally.Name: Wesley Thornberry - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Wesley Thornberry is a visionary leader and a driving force behind the inception and ongoing success of the Rally for Rangers project of the Mongol Ecology Center. As an ardent motorcyclist and conservation enthusiast, Wesley co-founded the Rally for Rangers and has been instrumental in elevating its profile on the global stage. Since 2014, he has actively participated in all 13 rallies, using his passion for adventure to draw international attention to the preservation of Mongolia's National Parks. In addition to his conservation efforts, Wesley is the founder and CEO of Trend Digital LLC, a renowned company specializing in post-production imaging services tailored to the e-commerce clothing and fashion industry. Wesley is a seasoned photographer, adventurer, and world traveler, having explored over 80 countries. His lens has captured the indigenous tribes of Ethiopia's Omo Valley to the mesmerizing depths of underwater national parks worldwide. He currently lives in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

Riders by Rally.#: 2024  —  National Parks of Bhutan  (14 riders)

Riders by Rally.Name: Ali Sarraf
Riders by Rally.Bio: Originally from Iran, I moved to Germany at the age of 15 and spent the most formative years of my life there before relocating to the US in my early thirties. I completed my high school and university studies in Bochum, a city in the heart of Germany’s old coal and steel region, and later began working in the IT industry. Over the last 30 years, I have worked on large-scale IT system implementations, giving me the opportunity to travel across the Americas, Europe, Asia, and Australia. I currently serve as a managing partner at Reply, a technology consulting firm based in Italy. As a child growing up in Iran, I dreamt of owning and riding a motorcycle, but wasn’t allowed to (some of my friends had 50cc and 80cc bikes in middle school). In 1999, I finally realized that dream, obtained my motorcycle license, and bought my first motorcycle – a 250cc Honda Rebel. Thanks to a dear friend with decades of experience in travelling by motorcycle, I quickly discovered my passion for long-distance moto travel. About 25 years ago, we began taking annual motorcycle trips together, and occasionally with other friends, exploring much of Western, Central, and Northern Europe, as well as parts of South America and North Africa. We have also done a few rides across the US. Joining rallies with Rally for Rangers allows me to combine my passion for motorcycle travel with contributing to a worthy cause and being part of a special community. It has been a privilege to be involved with this remarkable group of people.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bill Marsh - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Bill Marsh is a father of three living in Grand Rapids, Michigan, USA. He works in the packaging industry as a Key Accounts Manager for Hood Container and is a graduate of Michigan State University. He has travelled much of the continental US via motorcycle and enjoys international travel. Bill enjoys many outdoor activities including hiking, biking, fishing, golf, and especially exploring on a motorbike.

Riders by Rally.Name: Casey Mahon - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: I’m a dude from Cali, living in Prague, CZ for the last 24 years. Travelling a lot in EU for work and pleasure. I consider myself a recovering business-man that as an owner operator managed an import business bringing gifts and promotional items from India, Thailand, Nepal, China, Hong Kong and Taiwan. Traveling to all these places I have extensive travel experience in Asia. I’m a parent with two amazing young adult children at Uni in Prague. Dance and music in the Ecstatic Dance community are passions. As an Ecstatic Agent for two top international DJ’s I travel to events and festivals in Czech and around Europe. For work, I'm a consultant, investor and advisor in the area of decentralized finance. Finally I have a dog I love to bits. Noah is 14 years old and my example of how to live well. He always patient, kind, cautious, ready to play, has good boundaries, generous with showing love, a reliable companion and friend, finally we share the preference to be leashed or tied up only when necessary. These consistent qualities I aspire to and practice with dedication to my evolving spirit and soul. With the inspiration from Noah and another guru I’m making my way in this life. I hope that’s enough. Just Love 🧡

Riders by Rally.Name: Craig Hedges - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: A retired dad of two boys and a wonderful wife of 30 years looking for some adventures and excitement while I still can. Avid tennis player and golf enthusiast with a plan to take more motorcycle trips around the world.

Riders by Rally.Name: Craig Murray - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: "I am a longtime supporter of conservation efforts. I believe the future of our planet is a shared responsibility that we can’t take lightly. Visiting Peru in 2019, I was struck by the diverse beauty and rich cultural heritage of the land. But I was also struck by how fragile it is. I am also a longtime lover of motorcycles and motorcycle adventures. I’ve been riding for decades. I’ve ridden through most of the United States and half of the Canadian provinces, from the Atlantic to the Pacific, Gulf of Mexico to the Arctic Ocean. On road or off, it’s the best way to see any country. When I heard about Rally for Rangers and the work they do, I had to be part of it. What an amazing way to combine two passions into one philanthropic endeavor! I’m honored to have this opportunity to help rangers in Bhutan protect its precious lands." Craig is joining his second Rally for Rangers, following Peru 2022.

Riders by Rally.Name: Ed B. Medlin - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Ed began riding and racing motocross at age 12, then expanded to various other types of racing and road riding. In his 50’s Ed added automobile racing to his hobbies. Ed continues to ride motorcycles regularly, although mostly on dirt. Last year Ed rode down S. America from Buenos Aires through the Andes and Patagonia to the southern tip of S. America. In the past few months Ed did a 4 week , 4,000 mile motorcycle ride circling the western U.S., mostly on dirt.

Riders by Rally.Name: Erich Rainville - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: I've been a passionate rider for over 17 years, and in the last 7 years, my journey has taken an adventurous turn. I bid farewell to my sport bike and embraced the thrill of adventure riding. Exploring the rugged backcountry mountain roads of the Appalachian mountains in Virginia and West Virginia, conquering the majestic Rocky Mountains in Colorado, and navigating the sand dunes of North Carolina’s Outer Banks has been an exhilarating experience. In 2021, I proudly completed the MidAtlantic Backcountry Discovery Route (MABDR), a ride that not only tested my skills but also deepened my love for the open road. The last two years, my two wheels will carried me through the Northeast and Colorado BDRs. But more importantly, I joined Rally for Rangers for the first time to deliver motorcycles in Bhutan. Following that, I rallied to support the Native rangers of the Black Hills in South Dakota. These have eye-opening experiences, and it strengthened my belief in the mission of Rally for Rangers. I have witnessed firsthand the positive impact that motorcycles can have on the lives of rangers, providing them with the means to patrol vast and challenging terrains. What makes this year even more special is my return to Bhutan. Having previously explored the enchanting landscapes of Bhutan, I am eager to once again experience its unique beauty and immerse myself in the rich culture that the country has to offer . This upcoming rally will mark my third participation, and I am honored to contribute to the cause. I deeply believe in the mission of Rally for Rangers and the transformative effect it has on the lives of those who protect our precious natural resources.

Riders by Rally.Name: Lester Appel - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Lester Appel is the owner, operator, and President of Apple Elevator Company, a California corporation. As the founder of the company in 1983 Lester brings decades of trade knowledge to his firm. Lester is a 72 year old father of 3 and grandfather of 2. Born in Chicago Illinois, Lester grew up in Illinois and went to High School in St.Louis Missouri before moving west to Oakland California in 1978. While currently living in both Oregon and Arizona as a retired member of the IUEC (International Union of Elevator Constrctors) he continues to operate his Oakland California based company which employs his son, now in line to some day take over the business. Lester’s hobbies include motorcycles, windsurfing, snowboarding, hiking and gardening. He is a recent participant in the 2023 Rally for Rangers in the Gobi Desert and looks forward to the upcoming ride in Bhutan.

Riders by Rally.Name: Scott Gibson - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Scott currently resides with his partner and 4 dogs in La Crosse Wisconsin where he manages 3 short term rentals, sells aerial photos and coaches CrossFit. He started riding motorcycles in 1991 but never really put on too many miles as his adventure of choice for many years while living in Colorado was hiking in the foothills near Boulder. He spent 17 years in Colorado earning two Masters Degrees (Writing and Poetics/Curriculum and Instruction), hiking, teaching high school English and raising 3 adopted sons as a single dad. When life rattled some things loose in 2009, he took his kids to Costa Rica for about a year where he spent his time homeschooling and riding a 125cc dual sport on gravel hills, often weaving around potholes, snakes, monkeys and standing water 2-up (and sometimes even 3-up). One of his greatest feats was riding the moto 6 km on the Costa Rican roads with a cake for his son’s 14th birthday. When he landed back in the states, adventure was tattooed in his soul. He craved discovery off the beaten path, long stretches of traffic-free roads, and long days in the saddle — sounds cliche but there’s no other way to say it. He bought his first adventure touring bike in 2012 and took his 12 year old son on a moto camping trip from Wisconsin to Colorado. He was hooked. He has since taken several trips on various KTM’s through the west and southwest. Scott joined Rally for Rangers on their first North American rally in the black hills of South Dakota in September of 2023. It was the classic weather scenario…in the 70s upon arrival and departure, but a rainy 40’s and 50’s during the rally. What hooked Scott in to RfR’s mission was seeing the speechless appreciation of the Lakota rangers upon receiving their night vision gear donated by RfR. Scott is excited to join Rally for Rangers in Bhutan for his first international rally.

Riders by Rally.Name: Sean Anderson - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Sean was born and raised in the small town of Rupert, West Virginia. With an inherent curiosity of the outdoors and Tintin inspired lust for adventure, Sean dreamed of exploring as much of the world as he could. As a teenager, Sean spent countless hours browsing through his family’s home computer copy of Encarta ‘95, fueling his desire for education through experience. Sean is a Veteran of the United States Army and served a 13 month tour of duty in Iraq from ‘03-‘04. Uncomfortable experiences taught Sean the importance and value of empathy, and inspired a calling to selfless service. Sean currently works for Yosemite National Park. Sean was introduced to Rally for Rangers in 2017, by Tom Medema, and he’s been dreaming of the opportunity to participate in a Rally himself. Sean spends much of his free time in the Sierra Nevada, either hiking, camping or riding his Honda CB500X. In 2022, Sean rode 2,500 kilometers of northern Vietnam’e remote trails and roads. To date, Sean has visited 37 countries and each one has imparted vital knowledge and experience to him. Sean is honored to have been selected for a Rally and is elated to help support the Rally for Rangers mission of empowering park rangers all over the world.

Riders by Rally.Name: Steve Zuschin - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: "I was born and raised in Santa Cruz, California. But don't hold that against me, I learned an incredible appreciation for nature here. I've spent time living in and riding motorcycles in Portland OR, Chico CA, Brooklyn NY, Atlanta GA and currently reside on the South Shore of Boston MA. I'm an avid hiker, runner, and camper and am so in love with our state and national parks here in the US. I fell in love with two wheels, as early as I can remember, starting out with BMX bikes and taking advantage of motors whenever possible. I love riding, all kinds of riding, and do by best to get as many hours in the saddle as possible. I studied finance in college and have built a career in software sales in financial services, primarily working with startups that serve financial advisors with automated solutions. My amazing wife and 3 daughters encourage my motorcycle habit and great outdoor adventures and I'm forever grateful for their support."

Riders by Rally.Name: Thomas Burge - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Thomas Burge is a retired business executive and logistics consultant from Santa Cruz, CA. With a reduced workload and more freedom to travel, he has developed a passion for giving back. He is spending his time exploring philanthropic opportunities that align with his values, seeking ways to contribute to causes that promote compassion, mindfulness, and community well-being . The Rally for Rangers project in Bhutan accomplishes a tremendous crossroads for Tom to participate and develop his interests.

Riders by Rally.Name: Tim Burke - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: Upon hearing of Rally for Rangers via podcasts- I knew I was destined to join this adventure! The opportunity to participate in this great cause- AND ride a motorcycle was kismet! My motorcycle passion started with a ferocious Honda Spree Scooter- it was 50cc of pure rebellion. Evel Knievel was my childhood hero- and this was my gateway bike. I currently ride a 1961 BMW R50- and Suzuki DR650. I live in Lincoln NE- working in the wine business- I am also a host for The Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride-and founder of the Cluricaun Irish Society. I am beyond honored to join the Rally for Rangers team in this journey of a lifetime. An avid motorcyclist- the Rally for Rangers trip to Bhutan will be his 3rd Rally- joining Peru and the Black Hills.

Riders by Rally.Name: Tony Andes - 2024
Riders by Rally.Bio: The love of two wheels and independence can be traced to my early childhood. I remember being immersed in the activity and simply enjoying , whether on a bicycle or later a motorcycle. And to this day I still feel like that young kid every time I cycle or motorcycle. I have had the pleasure of enjoying various skill sets of motorcycle riding from wood riding to club road racing, but the memories and journeys of adventure riding have trumped them all. The ability to tour and ride in areas many people won’t drive or see is just incredible to me. And deepens my love of the sport and the outdoors. While at an offroad rally I learned of RfR, and instantly was drawn to the mission of the organization. The ability to help a cause and participate in an activity I love, seemed I needed to understand more. I am grateful to be able to participate and truly thank my wife for her support of my habit.

Riders by Rally.#: 2025  —  Great Gobi A National Park - Mongolia  (10 riders)

Riders by Rally.Name: Ali Sarraf
Riders by Rally.Bio: Originally from Iran, I moved to Germany at the age of 15 and spent the most formative years of my life there before relocating to the US in my early thirties. I completed my high school and university studies in Bochum, a city in the heart of Germany’s old coal and steel region, and later began working in the IT industry. Over the last 30 years, I have worked on large-scale IT system implementations, giving me the opportunity to travel across the Americas, Europe, Asia, and Australia. I currently serve as a managing partner at Reply, a technology consulting firm based in Italy. As a child growing up in Iran, I dreamt of owning and riding a motorcycle, but wasn’t allowed to (some of my friends had 50cc and 80cc bikes in middle school). In 1999, I finally realized that dream, obtained my motorcycle license, and bought my first motorcycle – a 250cc Honda Rebel. Thanks to a dear friend with decades of experience in travelling by motorcycle, I quickly discovered my passion for long-distance moto travel. About 25 years ago, we began taking annual motorcycle trips together, and occasionally with other friends, exploring much of Western, Central, and Northern Europe, as well as parts of South America and North Africa. We have also done a few rides across the US. Joining rallies with Rally for Rangers allows me to combine my passion for motorcycle travel with contributing to a worthy cause and being part of a special community. It has been a privilege to be involved with this remarkable group of people.

Riders by Rally.Name: Andre Schenk
Riders by Rally.Bio: I'm André Schenk, a Brazilian with a lifelong passion for travel and, even more so, for riding motorcycles. Exploring new places on two wheels is a way of experiencing the world, embracing challenges, and connecting with different cultures. I'm honored to contribute and be part of the Rally for Rangers Mongolia.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bryon Majusiak
Riders by Rally.Bio: Growing up in Reno, NV, Bryon took full advantage of the outdoors. Hiking, camping, fly fishing, and mountain biking filled his childhood, and it wasn't until he moved to Berkeley, CA, for college that he got his first taste of motorcycles. While at UC Berkeley, Bryon helped to build the world's first autonomous motorcycle, Ghostrider. Working on that project got him hooked on motorcycles for life. One bike led to 2, then 3, and is currently at 9, although most of them don't currently work (but will soon.) In 2013, he completed an Iron Butt ride around Nevada and still looks for any opportunity to take on a new challenge or adventure on a motorcycle. When not spending time working on motorcycles and cars, Bryon has a real job working at a company building agricultural robots. After watching "The Long Way Round," Bryon put Mongolia on the top of his bucket list of places to travel. It was a quick decision to join Rally for Rangers after finding out he could ride motorcycles and do something valuable for the national parks of Mongolia and across the world. Bryon has participated in multiple rallies in Mongolia, Namibia, and Nepal.

Riders by Rally.Name: Jeffrey Noel Takle
Riders by Rally.Bio: Jeff has been riding for twenty years and own an electric Zero SR/F, three off-road dirt bikes, and a sweet little Honda 150 dual sport. I was a captain in the U.S. Marine Corps and have travelled to 60 or more countries. I started a healthcare company in Nigeria and a nanotechnology company with MIT in Boston. Play the guitar, ski, cycle, bike and hang out with my kids, wife, dog, and cat.

Riders by Rally.Name: Josh Cohen
Riders by Rally.Bio: Josh Cohen resides in Southern Oregon’s Applegate Valley with his seventeen-year-old son Everett and thirteen-year-old daughter Ava, where he has owned and operated a certified organic vegetable farm for the past eighteen years. He was first introduced to the world of motorcycles at age eight by his father, and over the following eleven years, they spent more weekends than not exploring the deserts of California on dirt bikes. After taking a break for more than 25 years from riding, Josh obtained his motorcycle endorsement, and purchased a small dual sport motorcycle with which to camp off of and explore the more remote regions of Oregon and California with. Before becoming a farmer, Josh worked as a restoration ecologist for ten years in Santa Cruz and Monterey counties in California, with a focus on preserving rare and endemic plant and insect species. The opportunity to combine his passion for deserts, motorcycle travel, and conservation has him very excited to visit Mongolia’s Gobi Desert with Rally for Rangers in 2025!

Riders by Rally.Name: Maximilian Grant
Riders by Rally.Bio: Max is a veteran (I.e., former semi-professional camper) who has been riding for more than 40 years. The son of immigrants, he resides in Northern Virginia with his wife of 32 years, Maggie. His passion for motorcycling extends to all types of riding (scooters to MX to ADV to Iron Butt) and he has a national endurance road racing championship to his name, as well as moto tours of Iceland, Tasmania, the Alps and the Pyrenees.

Riders by Rally.Name: Nasanjargal Namsrai
Riders by Rally.Bio: Nasanjargal (Nasaa) is a petroleum engineer with over 25 years of experience. He currently serves as the COO of Petrovis Energy Group LLC, one of Mongolia’s leading energy companies. Under his leadership, Petrovis has proudly supported Rally for Rangers since 2018, providing essential support to rangers working in national parks across Mongolia. This is his fifth rally in Mongolia.

Riders by Rally.Name: Richard Thielmann
Riders by Rally.Bio: Richard “Rick” Thielman is a lifelong resident of Santa Barbara, California. He is a retired construction diver and supervisor who has been motorcycle riding for 55 years, for fun and in organized events up to the national level. His family (wife Susie, and three children) have all learned to ride and participated in his interest full time which required the appropriate fleet of vehicles for family off-road riding. Rick also has more specialized bikes as well as a street bike all the time. The local forest, American deserts, Sierra Mountains, Rocky Mountains, and Northwest area of America were all traversed. He is looking forward to a new experience, and riding in Mongolia with Rally for Rangers.

Riders by Rally.Name: Steven Croft
Riders by Rally.Bio: Steven participated in the Mongolian 2023 and 2024 Rally for Rangers and is back for his third Rally for Rangers. His riding journey began with an old orange Yamaha AG175 2-stroke, gifted by his dad in the late 1970s when he was just 14. Since that exhilarating start, Steven's passion for riding has taken him through various terrains and bikes, from enduro and trials to road and now adventure riding. " I participated in the 2023 and 2024 Mongolian Rally and thoroughly enjoyed the whole experience, and it was a high point of my year. It was very well run and managed, and now looking forward to doing it again in 2025 with some 2023 and 2024 friends and new people and riding in a different part of Mongolia. Can't wait for it. At home, I'm still riding Suzuki DR650 and V-Strom 1000, plus an HD Fat Bob and enjoy adventure riding in Australia, mainly around SE Queensland and Northern NSW.”

Riders by Rally.Name: Stuart Thielmann
Riders by Rally.Bio: Stuart grew up riding dirtbikes, from dry desert lake beds to high mountain trails in California. He first started on a Honda 50 with training wheels and graduated in bike sizes with age. This will be his first Rally and joined by his dad Rick. He is looking forward to the open landscapes and clear skies Mongolia has to offer. Stuart's other interests are outdoor sports and include rock climbing, surfing, hiking with his dog, and wandering with a camera in hand.

Riders by Rally.#: 2025  —  Nam Poui National Protected Area - Laos  (9 riders)

Riders by Rally.Name: Bill Marsh - 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: Bill Marsh is a father of three living in Grand Rapids, Michigan, USA. He works in the packaging industry as a Key Accounts Manager for Hood Container and is a graduate of Michigan State University. He has travelled much of the continental US via motorcycle and enjoys international travel. Bill enjoys many outdoor activities including hiking, biking, fishing, golf, and especially exploring on a motorbike. This is Bill's second rally.

Riders by Rally.Name: Douglas Wolf 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: I grew up in Maryland and now call Chicago home (though I’m not home too often). I helped found and operate an outdoor adventure summer camp for children, in Colorado, before retiring a few years ago, and since then have enjoyed more frequent motorcycle trips — in the US and especially abroad. I also enjoy hiking, camping, mountain biking and international travel with my wonderful wife and our two adult sons. I am inspired by the Rally for Rangers mission and look forward to participating in my first rally, in Laos, this year.

Riders by Rally.Name: Graham Cashwell 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: The motorcycle bug bit him in 1984 when he was a Peace Corps Volunteer in Liberia, West Africa. Riding amidst the challenges of unpaved roads and changing seasons, Graham's initiation into motorcycling was nothing short of a thrilling ride. The idea of adventure riding was introduced to him while traversing Mali, where he crossed paths with the iconic Paris Dakar Rally. This electrifying encounter set his spirit on fire, a spark that still burns bright. Graham's ride of choice now includes a BMW F800 GSA and a KTM 350 EXC-F – machines built to conquer uncharted paths. From BDRs (Backcountry Discovery Routes) to Baja and the rugged terrains of West Virginia, Graham finds solace in the embrace of the open road. Born and raised in the captivating landscapes of Richmond, VA, his heart found home in the allure of the world. With a life that's been lived around the globe, he's woven his experiences into every twist of the throttle. Beyond the road, his journey extends to the skies. A former military pilot turned airline captain, Graham's passion for flying is matched only by his love for two-wheeled exploration. And amidst it all, two remarkable adult children stand as a testament to the legacy he's building. Following his first Rally for Rangers, Mongolia 2023, he also joined Mongolia 2024 , Graham is not only seeking to ride, but to give back. His enthusiasm extends to working with fellow riders and the Mongol Ecology Center, a testament to his deep-rooted commitment to a greater cause.

Riders by Rally.Name: Jason Oliver - 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: Brewer, third-time Rally for Rangers rally participant, punster, historian, explorer, outlaw, imbiber, adventurer, cultural attaché, small dog owner, motorcycle enthusiast, philosopher, spiritual guru , and smart ass have been all words used to describe Jason Oliver. Most often by himself or when authorities are present. Jason Oliver's first foray into motor bikes was as a twelve year old in 1984 with a fourth hand Sears 2.5hp mini bike. He loved that thing. It had a metal plate that pressed against the rear wheel as a brake, it was sweet. Then came the 1977 Honda XL75 and the 1978 Honda XR80, alongside a slew of mopeds and scooters(Honda, Jawa, Tomos, ect). Anything he could work on while knowing absolutely nothing about mechanics. About 15 years ago he sold his beloved 2001 Kymco People 50 urban destroyer (aka The Silver Bullet) and moved from downtown Washington DC to the Blue Ridge mountains of Virginia. He immediately bought a used Suzuki DRZ 400 dual sport and began exploring the area which was an eye opener (to ride legally!!). His life changed again when he bought his first twin cylinder bike in 2016. He went down the rabbit hole of bigger is better and bought a BMW R1200 GSA. He put some serious miles on it. Crossing the country multiple times, an unofficial Iron Butt challenge, and taking it some places where he shouldn't have but managing to get out every time! Jason still loves large twins but his current favorite bike is a 2023 Honda CT125 Trail bike! If Rally for Rangers has taught him anything, it's that small bikes are a ton of fun and are way more practical in the real world than behemoths. He considers himself blessed to have both small & large displacement bikes, but if he had to choose, he'd pick a smaller bike like the ones donated by Rally for Rangers.

Riders by Rally.Name: Jim Britven  2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: Jim tuned into Adventure Rider Radio one day when he heard a story that caught his attention. The guest described a unique conservation organization leading an expedition to deliver motorcycles to wildlife rangers in Bhutan. The trip sounded exciting, purpose driven, and possibly a little dangerous. Jim’s first thought was ‘I wish I could do that; that trip sounds incredible.’ His second thought was ‘Why not try?’ So, this is him trying. Jim applied to the Rally for Rangers Laos expedition on short notice and with a long shot of being accepted. He was pleasantly surprised when he was asked to join. Previously, Jim was a Wilderness Ranger with the US Forest Service for several seasons in the White River National Forest. Since then, he has tried his hand at several careers, joined a startup, won some, and learned some. He is currently searching for the next meaningful way to spend his time. He is hopefully optimistic that the Rally for Rangers mission will scratch his itch for both purpose and adventure. This is Jim’s first Rally for Rangers and his first time riding off road. Hopefully it’s not his last.

Riders by Rally.Name: Lester Appel - 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: Lester Appel is the owner, operator, and President of Apple Elevator Company, a California corporation. As the founder of the company in 1983 Lester brings decades of trade knowledge to his firm. Lester is a 72 year old father of 3 and grandfather of 2. Born in Chicago Illinois, Lester grew up in Illinois and went to High School in St.Louis Missouri before moving west to Oakland California in 1978. While currently living in both Oregon and Arizona as a retired member of the IUEC (International Union of Elevator Constrctors) he continues to operate his Oakland California based company which employs his son, now in line to some day take over the business. Lester’s hobbies include motorcycles, windsurfing, snowboarding, hiking and gardening. He is a recent participant in the 2023 Rally for Rangers in the Gobi Desert and looks forward to the upcoming ride in Bhutan. This is his third rally.

Riders by Rally.Name: Mariam Appel - 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: From the Pacific Northwest of the U.S. not overly experienced on a motorcycle but looking forward to riding with my dad on this trip, and excited to get out more here in Oregon in preparation. It will be my first real multi-day ride and first in a foreign country. Excited for the adventure.

Riders by Rally.Name: Michael Emrich - 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: Michael (Mike) Emrich, now 75, has been riding since he was only 12 years old. He had traveled by motorcycle around the United States, twice to Alaska and Baja, Canada, Mexico, South America and Newfoundland. He began riding with Rally for Rangers in 2022 on the Bhutan rally. Since then, he joined the Namibia 2023 and Black Hills 2023 rally at the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota. In 2019, Michael embarked on an awe-inspiring journey from Cusco, Peru to Ushuaia, Argentina, covering a staggering 8,700 miles. Over half of the trip was spent conquering dirt, sand, gravel, and muddy roads. It's no surprise that Michael is still in top-notch shape and always ready for new challenges. " Retirement has given me the opportunity to give back to those less fortunate than myself and help with protect and save some of our environment and resources. Rally for Rangers provides the unique experiences of visiting those who you are helping while exploring the country your donation is helping. You also meet people who have similar goals. The group of people you get to travel with are amazing and so helpful." He has been married for 54 years with two beautiful children aged 48 and 45. He holds a BS from California Polytechnic University San Luis Obispo, CA. in Industrial Technology. In, 1975 he founded Solarponics , Inc an Atascadero, CA based Solar Energy, Radiant Heating and Energy Related Design and Installation Company.

Riders by Rally.Name: Steve Zuschin - 2025
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born and raised in Santa Cruz, California. But don't hold that against me, I learned an incredible appreciation for nature here. I've spent time living in and riding motorcycles in Portland OR, Chico CA, Brooklyn NY, Atlanta GA and currently reside on the South Shore of Boston MA. I'm an avid hiker, runner, and camper and am so in love with our state and national parks here in the US. I fell in love with two wheels, as early as I can remember, starting out with BMX bikes and taking advantage of motors whenever possible. I love riding, all kinds of riding, and do by best to get as many hours in the saddle as possible. I studied finance in college and have built a career in software sales in financial services, primarily working with startups that serve financial advisors with automated solutions. My amazing wife and 3 daughters encourage my motorcycle habit and great outdoor adventures and I'm forever grateful for their support.

Riders by Rally.#: UNASSIGNED  —  No Rally Assigned  (54 riders)

Riders by Rally.Name: Ahmet Shapey
Riders by Rally.Bio: I graduated from college with a degree in forestry and later studied environmental management at the Political Academy. I patrol 74 thousand hectares (183 thousand acres) of the Altai Tavan Bogd National Park. I love what I do as I contribute in preserving one of the most beautiful places.

Riders by Rally.Name: Altangerel Narantsetseg (Agy)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 43,900 hectares (~108,500 acres) of Otgontenger National Park, the north side of the Mount Otgontenger and the area around Bogd River. I graduated from college as a Tourism Manager in 2007 and joined the park in 2008. I have been working as a ranger for the 8 th year now.

Riders by Rally.Name: Altanginj Dugersuren (Ginj)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 50,700 hectares (~125,300 acres) of Tarvagatai Nuruu National Park. An ecologist by training, I have been working as a ranger for 5 years.

Riders by Rally.Name: Amarbayasakh Byambatsogt
Riders by Rally.Bio: He has been working as a ranger for 3 years in Lake Hovsgol National Park Administration. Amarbayasgalan protects 30 thousand hectares of land and aquatic squire of Lake Hovsgol. It covers Nutsgen Tolgoi, Jankhai’s hill, Bridge of Eg River and Soma Mountain both sides of west and east of the lake.

Riders by Rally.Name: Amgalan Yanjmaa
Riders by Rally.Bio: Born and raised in Altai, Amgalan used to herd his animals in the buffer zone of the National Park before becoming a part-time ranger in 2005 and then as a full-time ranger since 2010. Studied ecology at the University of Humanities in Ulaanbaatar. Lives with his wife and three children. Loves to spend his spare time in the repair shop. Facebook: Амгалан Янжмаа

Riders by Rally.Name: Azamat Sharivhan - 2018
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born at Sirgaali area of Altai Tavan Bogd National Park, which I now patrol and protect as a ranger. My homeland is wreathed by breathtaking scenery of the glacier, mountain peaks, wildlife and forest. In the 1990s, when Mongolia transitioned to democracy and capitalism, people started ripping off the nature by poaching and engaging in illegal logging. As I watched, my heart broke. My older brother worked in conservation for 40 years and he had a huge impact in my life. I started working as a ranger in 2001. Being a ranger helps me to give back. I am happy because I know that my work inspires my children.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bakhatbek
Riders by Rally.Bio: Prior to working as a ranger in 2015, I worked as a veterinarian. I graduated from the College of Agriculture in Hovd aimag. I patrol 74 thousand hectares (183 thousand acres) of the Altai Tavan Bogd National Park.

Riders by Rally.Name: Batjargal Dorj
Riders by Rally.Bio: He is an Ecologist. He has 28 years working experience for Nation and 20 years as a Ranger. He protects 110 thousand hectares of land and aquatic areas including from River of Kheeg Tsar to Bridge of Eg River.

Riders by Rally.Name: Batkhishig Davaadorj
Riders by Rally.Bio: His major is an ecologist and conservationist. He has been working as a ranger for 3 years for the Administration. Batkhishig protects 80 thousand hectares both land and aquatic areas. It includes from Dalbain Ovoot to Ar Balchirganat at Khankh soum.

Riders by Rally.Name: Batkhuu Baatarkhuu
Riders by Rally.Bio: Native to Selenge, Batkhuu had served in the military during 2009-2015. He started his career at Numrug National Park as a driver in 2018 and in 2020, he became a ranger. Married and has a son and a daughter. His wife Uuganbolor works as an assistant kindergarten teacher. On his very first patrol day, he saw a herd of Red Deer. And when he hid behind a tree, the herd came within two meters without noticing him. He was amazed and felt at the same time how important it is to keep these deer safe. He patrols 65018.92 hectares or 160665.2 acres of land. Batkhuu loves to wrestle and travel. Facebook: Батхүү Баатархүү

Riders by Rally.Name: Batmend Shiirev (Mend)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 28,910 hectares (~71,440 acres) around the south side of the Mount Otgontenger. I was born and grew up in the foothills of the Mount Otgontenger. When Otgontenger National Park was first established in 1996, I joined as a ranger and since then, I have been serving the park for 21 consecutive years. My duties as a park ranger include helping provide park services to over 3000 domestic and international visitors each year, ensuring their safety and interpreting Mongolian traditions of environmental stewardship, and preserving the State Worshipped Sacred Mountain of Otgontenger. I have many years of experience in wildlife conservation work, having completed numerous surveys on population, distribution and habitats of endangered animals and plants. During my career as a ranger, I have been named as the Best Officer in Environment and Tourism and have also received Certificates of Honor issued by the Ministry of Environment and Tourism and the Government of Mongolia.

Riders by Rally.Name: Batmunkh Hemjig - 2018
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol and protect 74 thousand hectares (183 thousand acres) of the Altai Tavan Bogd National Park. I have been working as a ranger since 2009. Alongside patrolling, protecting and promoting community participation, I contribute in biodiversity research and monitoring of the park.

Riders by Rally.Name: Battsagaan Batsukh
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born and raised in Myangad soum. I have a degree in geology, and since 2017, I have been working as a ranger at Khar Us Lake National Park. I patrol 70 thousand hectares (over 170 thousand acres) along Hovd River which is the main tributary of Khar Us Lake and home to endangered species such as wild boar, Asian beaver, and common pheasant.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bilegdemberel Lkhagva
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born and raised in Dörgön soum on the shorelines of Dörgön River. I got married in 1998, and we have four children. My wife is a doctor. I am proud to be a ranger, and I’ve been working in the park for 19 years. I patrol 110 thousand hectares (over 270 000 acres) of the park that include Akbash Island. The area of Akbash Island covers in 400 sq. meters and the main site for migratory pelicans and other endangered birds.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bold Banzai
Riders by Rally.Bio: Bold’s major is an Ecologist. He has an experience for 12 years its 4 years he has been working as a Ranger at the Park Administration. Bold’s protecting land cover 140 thousand hectares both squire of land and aquatic areas. The lands cover River of Taana and River of Noyon.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bold Byambajav
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born and grew up in Buyant soum of Hovd aimag. After serving in the Army, I worked as a veterinarian until 1998. Since that year, I have been working as a ranger. I patrol 165 thousand hectares (over 400 thousand acres) – all five tributaries of Khar Us Lake. My daily duties include monitoring and enforcing the legislation, educating the public and assisting visitors.

Riders by Rally.Name: Bujinlkham Tumurbaatar (Bujin)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 43,700 hectares (~108,000 acres) of Tarvagatai Nuruu National Park. I am a lawyer by training. In 2013, I applied to become a ranger at Otgontenger National Park and have been serving for the 5 th year now. Although I lacked environmental background at first, I have always been proud of working in conservation. It’s because nature is a wonder itself. I am committed to continue working in conservation, helping others including my children realize our inherent duty to protect and love nature.

Riders by Rally.Name: Byambadalai Dandar
Riders by Rally.Bio: Byambadalai is a ranger in Khankh soum. He protects 18 thousand of aquatic squire and 157 thousand lands of Lake Hovsgol National Park. Byambadalai is an ecologist and working as a ranger for 4 years. He protects areas between Khongor Boosh’s river and Khavtsal’s hill at Khankh soum.

Riders by Rally.Name: Dashdemberel Choijiljav (Dembe)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 42,000 hectares (~103,800 acres) of Tarvagatai Nuruu National Park, the area around Ulaan Haalga side. I am an ecologist by training. Having served as a volunteer ranger in Aldarkhaan soum of Zavkhan aimag for a while, I joined Otgontenger National Park in 2004 and have been serving as a ranger since then for 13 consecutive years. As a ranger, I contribute in preserving the scenic natural beauty, wildlife and forests of my native land by improving local community participation in environmental stewardship and rehabilitation, through various measures taken to reduce soil erosion, such as forming groups of herder households to lessen pasture degradation and organizing workshops and trainings to introduce and explain about park mission, regulations and activities.

Riders by Rally.Name: Dashdondov Chuluunbaatar
Riders by Rally.Bio: Dashdondov has been working for a ranger for 3 years and his protection area includes 63 thousand hectares both land and aquatic areas for Lake Hovsgol National Park includes from Nuurt’s hill to River of Kheeg Tsar.

Riders by Rally.Name: Davaajargal Sodnom
Riders by Rally.Bio: Davaajargal has worked for 2 years as a Ranger and protecting 77 thousand hectare of land. It includes from River of Khankh, Olon Nuur to Baishint.

Riders by Rally.Name: Enkhee Galbadrakh
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born in Buyant soum in 1962. I got married in 1984 after serving in the Army for three years. I’ve been working as a ranger for 18 years at Khar Us Lake National Park. I patrol 90 thousand hectares (220 thousand acres) – a key site for migratory birds. I grew up as a herdsman, so I like to work with our local communities and educating them the importance of the park resources.

Riders by Rally.Name: Enkhtaivan Demberel
Riders by Rally.Bio: He is a ranger and Environmental Inspector in the Administration. He has 32 years working experience in a nation and 11 years as a ranger for the Administration. He protects 52 thousand hectares of land and aquatic area including from Jankhai’s hill to Khokh Ovs (Blue Grass).

Riders by Rally.Name: Galbadrakh Purev
Riders by Rally.Bio: I have been serving the park for ten years and patrolling 90 thousand hectares (220 thousand acres) of the park. My ancestors preserved this beautiful place for our generation; and to continue their legacy, I work as a ranger. I am a teacher by profession and had taught in Dörgön soum for seven years. I am proud to be a ranger and being able to stop illegal actions in the park, so this beautiful place is preserved for our children.

Riders by Rally.Name: Ganbat Tsolmon
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 98,000 hectares (~242,200 acres) of Ulaagchny Har Nuur National Park. I joined the protected areas administration three years ago. I am a vet by training and worked as one until 1997. While serving as the Head of Citizen’s Representative Assembly of Erdenekhairkhan soum of Zavkhan aimag in 2008-2012, I initiated the effort to take places of natural beauty and cultural heritage in the soum under local protection and ensured protective measures were taken. I joined the protected areas administration as a ranger 3 years ago.

Riders by Rally.Name: Gantulga Olonbayar - 2018
Riders by Rally.Bio: When I was growing up I always wanted to be a ranger, but I became a veterinarian. I went back to school to study environmental management so that I could pursue my childhood dream. I started working as a ranger in 2005 at the Altai Tavan Bogd National Park. I patrol 74 thousand hectares (183 thousand acres) which covers the biggest glacier of Mongolia, Potanin Glacier, and Shiveet Mountains and White River areas.

Riders by Rally.Name: Hishigbat Bayaraa
Riders by Rally.Bio: Growing up, I was told not to make the spirits of water angry by polluting the rivers and springs. The year that I graduated from secondary school, artisanal miners discovered gold in Altrag River, our main drinking water source. Before you know it, our river was turning into a black mud. That led me to organize a student movement to fight against illegal artisanal miners and it was a success. Ever since then, I have devoted my life to become a ranger and I am proud to say that there is no miner left in Bayanzurkh soum. I patrol 60,000 hectares [over 148 thousand acres] of the protected area.

Riders by Rally.Name: Khairat Amankeldy
Riders by Rally.Bio: I have been working as a ranger for 17 years since I graduated from the University of Agriculture. I live with my wife and four kids in Khuurait of Nogoon nuur (Green Lake) soum. I patrol the highest mountain area of the park, a critical site for snow leopard, black marmot, argali sheep, ibex, Altai eagle, and Altai snowcock.

Riders by Rally.Name: Khurgaa Chuluun
Riders by Rally.Bio: Khurgaa works as a ranger for Lake Hovsgol National Park locates in Khankh. He has 6 years working experience for a ranger. His protecting land covers 64 thousand hectares including from Khavtsal’s hill to River of Taana

Riders by Rally.Name: Marat Toley
Riders by Rally.Bio: My ancestors preserved this beautiful place so that I can enjoy it. To continue their legacy, I became a ranger in 2009. My job inspires me every day and I feel proud that I am a part of a big network of protected areas.

Riders by Rally.Name: Miiraa Urt
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 95,300 hectares (~235,500 acres) of Ulaagchny Har Nuur National Park, the area around Santmargad soum. I am trained in ecology in and environmental conservation. Before becoming a ranger at the administration in 2014, I served as a State Environmental Inspector in Dorvoljin soum of Zavkhan aimag.

Riders by Rally.Name: Munkh-Amdiral Gantumur
Riders by Rally.Bio: Born in Hentii province, worked in the mining industry before joining border troops in Numrog. Since his discharge in 2018 working at the national park as a ranger. His scope of work includes work with the public. He patrols 89349.82 hectares or 220788.2 acres of land. Married, has two daughters. His wife Bolorchimeg works as a bank teller. Munkh-Amidral used to play volleyball professionally, so whenever he gets a chance he loves to play and works as a referee. He also loves to travel and cook. He has been riding a motorcycle for 3 years. Facebook: Мөнх-Амьдрал Гантөмөр

Riders by Rally.Name: Naljirmaa Baljinnyam (Naljir)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 22,700 hectares (~56,000 acres) of Otgontenger National Park, the area around the Dayan Mountain. I am a landscape planning engineer by training. My uncle Davaadorj was a ranger here back in 2002-2008 and he used to patrol the area which I am currently responsible for. While helping him patrol and ensure that the Dayan Mountain was safe and free of garbage, I was inspired by his work ethic and developed a stronger sense of environmental stewardship. Years later when I retired, I applied to become a ranger and have been serving the park for 9 years now. I have been named as the Best Environmental Officer and I was awarded a Certificate of Honor by the Ministry of Environment and Tourism.

Riders by Rally.Name: Nyamkhuu Chogdon
Riders by Rally.Bio: Nyamkhuu’s major is an Agricultural mechanist. He has 25 years working experience for the State and 8 years as a ranger. He protects 84 thousand hectares of land and aquatic areas for Lake Hovsgol National Park including from Khokh Ovs (Blue Grass) to Ol.

Riders by Rally.Name: Oinbayar Lhachin
Riders by Rally.Bio: As he lived at the border of the national park when the Takhi reintroduction program started, in 1992, he used to help rangers to prepare hay and look after Takhi horses who were put in monitoring ranges. Went to university and graduated as an ecologist. Since 2007 he is working as a ranger. Lives with his wife and 3 kids. Has good mechanical skills, loves to read. Facebook: Л.Ойнбаяр Ойнбаяр

Riders by Rally.Name: Otgonjargal Palam
Riders by Rally.Bio: Otgonjargal protects 68 thousand hectare of land includes areas of Baishint, Toi, Shivdeg, Taankh and Olon Nuur. He has served 10 years for Nation and 2 years as a ranger.

Riders by Rally.Name: Purevee Batsuren
Riders by Rally.Bio: Purevee works as a Ranger and Environmental Inspector for the Administration in Khanh soum. His major is Forest and Hunt Technician. He has served 24 years for Nation and 5 years as a Ranger. Purevee protects 92 thousand hectares of land for Lake Hovsgol National Park from River of Noyon to Bridge of Borsogo.

Riders by Rally.Name: Rentsendorj Buriad (Rentsen)
Riders by Rally.Bio: I patrol 60,000 hectares (~148,300 acres) of Ulaagchny Har Nuur National Park. I have been a ranger for 3 years.

Riders by Rally.Name: Saldat Tahay
Riders by Rally.Bio: I worked as a veterinarian until 2001 in the area that I now patrol as a ranger. The Altai Tavan Bogd National Park was saved in 1996 when people started destroying its nature and beauty for their own greed. The director of the newly established park administration, A. Atai, offered me a job as a ranger so that we can contribute in protecting our homeland. Without looking back, I became a ranger. I work as a ranger so that our younger generation can enjoy and be inspired by my homeland.

Riders by Rally.Name: Sarantuya Soninbayar
Riders by Rally.Bio: I have been working as a ranger since 2009. I patrol 74 thousand hectares (183 thousand acres) which covers Bayanzurkh Mountain, Jiren, Dood Khaalgat and shorelines of the Lake Hurgan.

Riders by Rally.Name: Sodbileg Byambajav
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born and raised in Chandmani soum of Hovd aimag. I have a degree in Literature and Mongolian language. My dad influenced me to become a ranger. As a kid, I used to herd our sheep and goats and loved wandering out in the wilderness. It was important to me that the future generations get to enjoy nature as much as I did. Currently, I patrol and protect 87 thousand hectares (more than 210 thousand acres) of the park.

Riders by Rally.Name: Talgatbek Duan - 2018
Riders by Rally.Bio: I started working as a ranger when the government established the Altai Tavan Bogd National Park 22 years ago. The 74 thousand hectares (183 thousand acres) that I patrol are rich in cultural treasures such deer stones, funerary structures (Kheregsuur) and other archeological sites.

Riders by Rally.Name: Terbish Kolya
Riders by Rally.Bio: Native to Numrog, Terbish grew up locally. After getting a law degree in Ulaanbaatar he worked in the local administration of Halkhgol county before joining the park administration as a monitoring ranger in 2017. He patrols the entire park and operates a drone. In 2019 he was able to capture some rare footage of Red-Crowned Cranes in the park, endangered worldwide with only 2700 of them remaining. He is married and has a son. He loves to read books, photographing, and making videos. He has been riding a motorcycle for 4 years. Facebook: Terbish Kolya

Riders by Rally.Name: Tolegen Kaden
Riders by Rally.Bio: I’ve been a ranger at Siilkhem Mountain National Park since 2004. End of the 1990s, Mongolia’s natural resources were depleted by wrongdoers. The population of argali sheep and Altai marmot decreased rapidly. It was tragic. Fortunately, the government took the area under protection in 2000, and after some hard work, the population of argali sheep has grown to 1600-1800.

Riders by Rally.Name: Tsegmid Sandui
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born in 1972 at Mankhan soum. I live with my wife and two kids in Mankhan soum. Before working as a ranger, I worked as a driver, tax inspector, and representative of a local council. Since 2017, I have been working as a ranger and patrolling over 115 thousand hectares (285 thousand acres). I am proud of preserving rare and endemic species such as Mongolian Saiga antelope. My life goal is to protect these beautiful species for our children’s children.

Riders by Rally.Name: Tserendavaa Tseveen
Riders by Rally.Bio: I was born and raised in Chandmani soum. A year ago, I became a ranger. I patrol 96 thousand hectares (237 thousand acres) of the park. I’ve been a herdsman for 22 years, so I know the land well.

Riders by Rally.Name: Tsogtbayar Gombo
Riders by Rally.Bio: Tsogtbayar Gombo has been the chief ranger and environmental inspector of Lake Hovsgol National Park for 5 years.

Riders by Rally.Name: Ukhnaa Gundjii
Riders by Rally.Bio: Ukhnaa is an ecologist. He has served for 20 years for Nation and 12 years as a Ranger. He protects 173 thousand hectares both land and aquatic areas which includes from Ol’s hill to Khongor Boosh’s River. His protecting areas is the bigger than other rangers.
